fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 cannot make every signed nonpermutation polynomially farther. For any linear Euclidean realization with cheap permutations P1,P2,P3, a signed nonpermutation T=P1+P2-P3 has squared distance at most nine times the common legal squared radius by the triangle inequality; changing the Gram matrix does not escape this constant-factor ceiling.

Proposal 2 supplies neither an explicit selector matrix nor a protected-center cost calculation. Testing whether small hashes isolate matchings does not test the actual obstruction, while the existing global-branch experiment already admits a weight-9 rectangle splice; any proposed escape must specify and attack the complete syndrome fiber.

Proposal 3 is incompatible with binary linearization: three cheap legal fillings XOR to another target-fiber word of weight at most three times the legal cost. Nonabelian labels or Fox derivatives do not prevent this after conversion to a binary boundary matrix; enforcing reduced-word validity nonlinearly would require an unprovided, potentially exponential representation.

Proposal 4 has an implementation trilemma. Whole-path columns enumerate exponentially many assignment paths, edge columns cannot linearly encode noncommutative path products, and flow/tableau enforcement re-enters O2; noncommutative identity testing also preserves nonzeroness rather than Hamming support, the exact failure seen for prior condensers.

Proposal 5 has no polynomial parameter regime: fixed truncation degree is covered by bounded-degree cube relations, while growing degree generally creates n^D Macaulay monomials and becomes superpolynomial before supplying logarithmic/global soundness. The target homology class and precise differential are also unspecified, so the proposed finite computation would not test a complete reduction.

Proposal 6 is not a lattice construction because binomial(z_j,2) is nonlinear in lattice coefficients. Linearizing it with monomial variables either returns to bounded-degree cube cancellations or requires a growing monomial dictionary, while spanning lifted Boolean fiber points requires finding or enumerating the NP-hard fiber.

Proposal 7 has the same affine-combination ceiling as Proposal 1. Three low-cost legal permutation routings linearly combine to a signed nonpermutation routing with squared congestion at most nine times the worst legal cost, and the q log q legal routing baseline already prevents logarithmic replication from producing a polynomial ratio.
evidence: All seven proposals are explicitly marked untested; no supplied verifier establishes any claimed separation for them.

The obstruction map proves bounded-degree signatures, marginal/tableau interfaces, and bounded-fan-in linearizations retain exact short trades, directly covering the fallback implementations in proposals 3–6.

Existing selector evidence found a weight-9 rectangle splice, and affine-closure verification found 32 instances where an illegal cover lies in the affine span of legal matchings. These are concrete warnings against proposals 2 and 3, not asymptotic extrapolations.

Prior noncommutative and dense-fold verifiers preserved orientation or nonzeroness but failed support separation: M3(F4) produced NO kernels, and the F8 condenser had worst YES 31 versus best NO 6. Proposal 4 supplies no theorem or structural mutation addressing that rank-to-support failure.

The direct permutation-table construction already achieved only additive 12 versus 14, and the determinant/all-compound mutation retained short virtual permutations. Proposals 1 and 7 do not escape the underlying linear affine-combination bound.

Reopen only after supplying an explicit polynomial-size matrix whose columns are computable without enumerating witnesses, together with a proof-level reason that signed combinations of three cheap legal representations cannot yield a cheap target-fiber word; then precommit one exact all-eight, affine-closure, holonomy, and all-mixed-word test.

fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 does not define how a local triple column evaluates genuinely global assignment monomials. Using only information carried by that triple returns to bounded local signatures; adding product consistency returns to tableaux/moments; using complete assignments is exponential. The cover-free family, tie-breaking, BCH map, target, and resulting binary matrix are also unspecified, so the proposed finite test is not reproducible.

Proposal 2 has no completeness mechanism connecting a satisfying assignment to trivial nonabelian transport. Formula-fixed labels cannot depend on the witness, while witness-dependent transports require an unspecified global selector or multiplication tableau; moreover fixed S3 supplies only constant conjugate spreading, not a polynomial gap.

Proposal 3 has no linear construction implementing acceptance of one protected sector without either charging every sector or introducing an OR/branch interface. Isolation of a legal minimum does not by itself separate illegal affine superpositions, and the proposed enumeration omits a defined combiner matrix and target.

Proposal 4 asks additive columns to measure the rank or Plücker profile of a selected set, which is nonlinear across selected triples. Linearizing those wedges requires subset columns or product-consistency interfaces, while per-triple compounds do not compute the compound of the selected collection. No endpoint-vector normalization establishes uniformly cheap YES witnesses.

Proposal 5 supplies neither a specific Lawrence matrix, expander, target, nor norm weights. Searching coefficients only in [-2,2] cannot certify an integer-fiber minimum or absence of larger-coefficient Graver repairs, so its proposed experiment is not genuinely discriminating.

Proposal 6 is already algebraically defeated: the recorded all-eight and holonomy mixed words cancel every indexed walk feature before coding. Any linear prefix or tree-code transform maps that zero feature vector to zero, and bounded occurrence or orientation does not change this fact.

Proposal 7 needs growing degree to escape the fixed-degree obstructions, but the full squarefree Macaulay space through degree Theta(log n) has n^{Theta(log n)} size. No polynomial sparse monomial rule or multiplicity matrix is specified, and degree-3/4 tests cannot discriminate the missing growing-degree construction; evaluation-vector Hamming baselines are also assignment-dependent.
evidence: The bounded-signature theorem gives exact alternating cube relations that survive arbitrary linear rows, modular reduction, and dense postprocessing. Cover-free design properties concern set isolation and do not invalidate XOR finite-difference relations.

The existing walk verifier found an all-eight illegal mixed word of cost 6 and a twisted-holonomy illegal word of cost 9, with every walk coordinate zero. This directly falsifies the claimed tree-code protection mechanism rather than merely providing adverse finite statistics.

The exchange-quotient verifier found illegal odd covers in the affine span of perfect matchings on 32 instances. Separate cheap sectors therefore require a non-affine, explicitly encoded selector; no such selector appears in Proposal 3.

The determinant/exterior verifier retained support-three virtual permutation states even after all compound coordinates were added, while the explicit global dictionary was exponential. This is direct adverse evidence for Proposal 4's rank-profile premise.

Integer exact-cover experiments obtained only additive gaps, including 12 versus 14 with variable projection tables, and proved that affine table interfaces impose linear YES baselines. Proposal 5 gives no mutation that removes this baseline or excludes constant toric repairs.

No verifier evidence is supplied for Proposals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 7, and none specifies a complete binary H,t instance whose full mixed fiber can be enumerated. Their finite sketches therefore cannot presently support implementation.
